x: After a brisk half-mile Giani was in the first dozen. Manning led our men with Green and Rathbone walking very easily in the middle of the field and our 4 others following.
Giani finished 5th, Pavesi 10th, and Brignoli, Rivolta Biondetti and some others fell by the roadside owing to the fierceness of the battle.

Green had just made his first attempt in the Brighton Walk and had finished second to the Italian, Giani. The Belgrave team (Green, Rathbone, Manning) was successful in the team race by one point, from Surrey Walking Club.

In 1927 Tommy Green, who later won the first Olympic 50 km Walk, began to carve a permanent place for himself in the history of the 'Brighton' when he finished 2nd to the 21 year old Italian Giani in 8hrs. 26mins. 44secs. and led the Club to victory in the team race.
